# Project folders and files

[Project home](../README.md) · [Folder guide](project_structure.md)

Start with run.py. Model parameters, prescribed excitation, experimental references and computed results have separate, descriptive folders. Each folder has a navigation guide.

| Path from project root | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`run.py`](../run.py) | Compute a NEW fully forward trial, optionally opening the result viewer. |
| [`view.py`](../view.py) | Open an already computed trial without recalculating it. |
| [`reproduce.py`](../reproduce.py) | Recompute the complete 60-second intact walking simulation. |
| [`Code/neuromechanics`](../Code/neuromechanics/README.md) | Functions that calculate excitation, activation, muscle and tendon forces, paw contact, coupled body motion and output comparisons. Each file represents a named part of the calculation. |
| [`Code/model_configuration`](../Code/model_configuration/README.md) | Code that defines parameter names, validates their organization and locates project files. To change physical values for a simulation, edit Data/Model_Parameters. |
| [`Code/simulation_tools`](../Code/simulation_tools/README.md) | Commands for running the model, playing its saved movement, exporting figures and preparing documentation. The root run.py is the normal entry point. |
| [`Data/Model_Parameters`](../Data/Model_Parameters/README.md) | Editable values for body mass and inertia, joints, muscle attachments, activation, muscle–tendon mechanics, contact and the initial state. Source-to-model tables explain the origin and applied value of each documented parameter. |
| [`Data/Muscle_Excitation_Input`](../Data/Muscle_Excitation_Input/README.md) | The excitation waveform supplied to every muscle channel. excitation_cycle.tsv stores one cycle of dimensionless commands between 0 and 1; the simulator repeats this cycle and computes activation from it. |
| [`Data/Experimental_Reference_Data`](../Data/Experimental_Reference_Data/README.md) | Joint angles, paw forces and EMG used to assess the prediction. RH is recorded, LH is an assumed mirror, and forelimb references come from a separate study. These curves do not drive the motion during a forward run. |
| [`Data/Original_Study_Data`](../Data/Original_Study_Data/README.md) | Original numerical tables and MATLAB files from the hindlimb and forelimb studies, retained to trace the scientific sources. The organized parameter and excitation files define the inputs used by run.py. |
| [`Data/Skeletal_Geometry`](../Data/Skeletal_Geometry/README.md) | The connected body and joint structure and its geometric data. This determines where forces act and how segments move. Optional bone surface meshes change the appearance, not the mechanical calculation. |
| [`Simulation_Results/Intact_Walking`](../Simulation_Results/Intact_Walking/README.md) | 60-second intact forward simulation, raw states and experimental comparisons. |
| [`Verification`](../Verification/README.md) | Executable equation checks and complete intact-walking reproduction. |
| [`Documentation/References`](References/README.md) | Scientific papers, citations and links to original sources. |
| [`Documentation/Figures_and_Videos`](Figures_and_Videos/README.md) | Scientific comparison plots, muscle schematics and walking animation. |
